newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay index falls 1.85 pct, ends near day's lows.
newsitem.headline: Bombay index falls 1.85 pct, ends near day's lows.

text.p: Bombay shares suffered fresh losses on Friday with a public holiday affecting trading volumes and fresh demand, brokers said.
"Institutions are not active in the market. This fall has taken everyone by surprise," said Sanjay Vaid, chief dealer at local firm, Lloyds Securities.
The absence of any fund activity ahead of the long Easter week-end and a holiday at the National Stock Exchange (NSE) gave bear operators the upper hand, dealers said.
The sell-off pulled down Bombay's top-30 index 69.24 points or 1.85 percent to provisional close of 3,666.34.
The end of the weekly trade account at the Bombay exchange also led to business-squaring by operators, dealers said.
"There might have been a lot of squaring-off of outstanding positions by market players near end of trade," said Ajit Ambani, a BSE member-broker.
"We feel bear operators have taken advantage of a dull day and hammered prices to create some sort of a shaky market mood," said an equities dealer at a foreign brokerage.
Trading volumes were low because of Good Friday holiday for banks, government offices and the NSE which operates from more than 100 centres across India, traders said.
"It has been really boring trading day. The market weakness near the close of the session lacked any fund based selling," the dealer at the foreign brokerage said.
Shares of shoe-maker Bata India ended 4.25 rupees, or 6.4 percent, higher at 71.0 rupees after the firm on Thursday announced profits.
Bata India unveiled a net profit of 41.5 million rupees for calendar 1996 against net loss of 421.6 million rupees in 1995.
